The paper establishes the exact electromagnetic field solution for a spherical invisibility cloak with an active device inside.
Extraordinary electric and magnetic surface voltages are induced at the inner boundary of the spherical cloak.
The surface voltages prevent electromagnetic waves from going out of the concealed region.
The phase and handness of polarized waves obliquely incident on the inner boundary are kept in the reflected waves.
The surface voltages are found to be exactly equal to the auxiliary scalar electric and magnetic potentials at the inner boundary.
For a static electric dipole inside, the electric surface voltage becomes zero while the magnetic surface voltage survives.
For a static magnetic dipole inside, the magnetic surface voltage becomes zero while the electric surface voltage survives.
The condition where the material at the inner boundary has radial permittivity and permeability of zero is sufficient for total reflection of all waves.
The special uniaxial medium at the inner boundary behaves like a perfect magnetic conductor for TM waves and a perfect electric conductor for TE waves.
The surface voltages support the discontinuity of the tangential electromagnetic fields across the inner boundary, even without conductive media or surface currents.
The time-averaged Poynting power inside the concealed region is zero, meaning no time-averaged power flows inside.
The field distribution inside the concealed region exists in the form of standing waves.
The surface voltages are induced by an infinite polarization of the material at the inner boundary.
The surface voltages can push a free charge at the interface and transfer energy to it.
The paper provides a rigorous mathematical treatment of the cloaking problem with an active device inside.
